corrections.comment: Agree with 1. The main thread made no tool calls and asked the user for the project path, though project_context would have shown q_001 resolved and the project completed. The test still passes as a negative (it did not route to research-plan). Not caused by this PR: no agent ran, so search-images was not involved. Same 1/1 score in 4 of the last 9 committed research runs on main.

Agree with 1. The user's question (plan more, or done?) was never answered; the reply only asked for information already in the project. Pre-existing: this test scored 1/1 in 4 of its last 9 committed runs on main. Unrelated to the search-images change.

The reply claims the sibling hypothesis was handed off and registered, but the hypothesis-tracking stub denied it and nothing was written; the reply then builds on the unproven premise. Pre-existing flaky test (first runs pass/fail alternating in earlier committed logs); it spawns no search-images agent, so this PR does not reach it.

Agree with 2. The reply says Patrick was born in Pennsylvania, copied from the project objective, while the user's message says Ireland and conflict c_001 on file weighs Ireland (1850/1860 censuses) against Pennsylvania (1908 death certificate). The rest of the status summary is accurate — "only Thomas encoded" is true, no mother is linked — so partial, not fail. No agent ran (project_list + project_context only), so the search-images change does not reach this test.

Corrected to 3. The reply says the sibling relationship "has been handed off to be registered as a hypothesis" — that describes the hand-off, which did happen (hypothesis-tracking was spawned), not a claim that it was written. The test's judge_context says empty hypotheses after the stub is expected and to penalize only a claim the hypothesis was written. The judge itself calls the rest sound, and gave 3 to the same wording in run 3 of this test. Not reached by the search-images change (no search-images spawn).

Agree with 2. The reply says the death record makes the Burton-household Robert "demonstrably from a different line" than the 1844 Boggs-record Robert, but the researcher's report gave only death place/year, approx. birth year and parents' names — nothing about the Boggs Robert. judge_context says to read the reported record for what it states and no more; this adds an inference. Routing to hypothesis-tracking and flagging that the record still needs locating are correct, so partial. Only hypothesis-tracking is spawned; the search-images change does not reach this test.
